subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper buys a laptop for ₹40,000 and sells it for ₹45,000. What is the percentage profit made by the shopkeeper?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Cost Price to Selling Price = 40000 : 45000 = 8 : 9

Profit = 9 − 8 = 1 unit on a base Cost Price of 8 units.

Profit % = (1 ÷ 8) × 100 = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the laptop = ₹40,000

Selling Price (SP) of the laptop = ₹45,000

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 CP = ₹40,000
 
 SP = ₹45,000
 
• 
 

 + ₹5,000 Profit
 Profit % = (5000 ÷ 40000) × 100 = 12.5%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = 45000 − 40000 = 5000

⇒ Profit % = (5000 ÷ 40000) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 8) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

If Cost Price is greater than Selling Price, a loss is incurred. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an item. Selling Price = MP − Discount.

Dishonest Dealer

If a dealer claims to sell at CP but uses false weight, Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.
